acceptance: IPFS follow-ups — the three INT-07 clauses A31 left open, plus the moderator-block ruling
closes: docs/release-readiness.md § A31 IPFS — public mirror with fallback, private swarm isolation — 2026-09-09, "What INT-07 still needs" items 1-5

verdict.INT-07: NOT FLIPPED HERE. This slice is code plus tests; the row moves on an A31 re-run against a real kubo topology, not on a merged PR.
delivered: a health-gated server-side redirect, with an `ipfs` component on /readyz and /admin/system
a runtime delivery_ipfs_enabled setting beside its two siblings
a reconcile pass that compares the ledger with the node in both directions
a moderator block that unpins and an unblock that re-publishes
a QoE event at the source switch

component.probe: HEAD (GET with Range on a non-2xx) of {IPFS_GATEWAY_URL}/ipfs/{cid} for the first pinned public CID in the ledger, in object-key order
component.why_not_rpc: A31 measured the daemon up with its gateway listener stopped: RPC answered, /ipfs/status read node_reachable=true, and every 307 died. They are different listeners and often different hosts.
component.cadence: on boot, then every 5 minutes — internal/storage.WriteHealth's cadence; the request path reads the record, never probes

states.not_configured: IPFS_ENABLED false, no IPFS_GATEWAY_URL, nothing pinned yet (no CID to ask for), or delivery_ipfs_enabled switched off
states.ok: the gateway served a CID this instance publishes
states.degraded: the gateway serves and pin operations have dead-lettered
states.down: the gateway did not serve, or the oldest due pin row is more than 2h overdue

component.readiness: never fails readiness — it sets the body's top line to degraded with a 200; only PostgreSQL 503s (health.go's existing rule)
component.role_note: the probe loop is NOT gated on runWorkers — the api role issues the redirects and runs no workers, so gating it like the drain loop would leave the deciding process with no evidence

redirect_gate.redirectable: Probed AND state == ok — an unprobed monitor refuses, because "we have not looked" is not evidence a viewer sent there gets bytes
redirect_gate.otherwise: the api serves the authoritative bytes; no 307 is minted

setting.default: IPFS_ENABLED (not false — gateway redirects are already what an IPFS-enabled instance does; defaulting off would be a behaviour change wearing a safety default's clothes)
setting.default_read_from: the process's own cfg, via the new instancesettings.Overridden — so a caller that forgets Defaults.IPFSEnabled cannot silently switch delivery off
gates: the `ipfs` object on GET /videos/{id} that draws the watch toggle
setting.does_not_gate: the card/feed ipfs_pinned badge, which is a fact about pinning rather than about delivery
setting.worker_role: the settings poller is role-gated, so a worker process keeps the value it booted with. That is correct here: this switch governs DELIVERY and a worker answers no media request. Pinning is governed by IPFS_ENABLED, which is env and restart-only on every role.

redirect_gate.doc_fix: delivery.WithMirror's comment claimed the per-request read let an operator turn the mirror off without a restart. The switch it read was cfg.IPFSEnabled, an env var. The comment now describes the real lever.

reconcile.entry: ipfsmirror.Service.VerifyPins, on the IPFS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL tick (default 5m), leader-only, beside Reconcile and SweepIneligible
algorithm: ask the node for every recursive pin in ONE call (ipfs.Client.ListPins)
walk one keyset page of that swarm's 'pinned' rows, resuming where the last tick stopped
a row whose CID the node does not hold is re-armed to 'pending' (RearmLostIPFSPin, guarded on state AND cid)
read every CID the ledger has a LIVE claim on and report any node pin in none of them

bounds.cursor: in-memory keyset on object_key — no migration; a restart costs at most one restarted cycle

reconcile.node_unreachable: ListPins errors and the sweep ends with NO writes. IsPinned cannot tell 'not pinned' from 'the node did not answer', so a reconcile built on it would re-add the whole ledger during an outage.
reconcile.strays: REPORTED, never removed. A kubo pin carries no marker separating a Vidra pin from an operator's own — add attaches no namespace and no name that survives into pin/ls — so an unpin here would be deleting data on a guess. The count rides on the `ipfs` component's detail as unaccounted_node_pins; -1 means no comparison completed, which is deliberately not 0.
reconcile.in_flight: the stray comparison is made against 'pinned', 'pending' AND 'unpinning' rows, so a CID the worker is accounting for right now is never accused

block_lifecycle.ruling: 2026-09-09 (owner): a moderator block, and quarantine, unpin the video's public CIDs like a privacy flip does; unblock re-arms the mirror so the CIDs are re-published.
block_lifecycle.why_a_new_fact: BlockVideo writes a video_blocks row and changes neither videos.privacy nor videos.state, so nothing the eligibility fence already read could see a block. A31 measured the consequence: a blocked video 404'd on every Vidra surface while its CIDs stayed retrievable from the gateway.

mechanism.fence: ipfsmirror.Subject.VideoBlocked; Route returns NetworkNone for a blocked video-derived class on BOTH swarms — a block is a removal decision, not a visibility one, so it does not fall through to the private swarm
mechanism.immediate: POST/DELETE /admin/videos/{id}/block call Service.SyncVideoCounted — the same seam a privacy flip uses; unpins are reference-count-guarded in the worker exactly as before
mechanism.backstop: SweepIneligibleIPFSPins gained an EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM video_blocks …) on branches 1 and 3, so the ledger converges on the next reconcile tick even if a hook was missed
mechanism.unblock: guarded on `lifted`, so a second idempotent DELETE does not re-arm a mirror nothing changed
mechanism.quarantine: entering quarantine needs no hook — 'quarantined' is not 'published' and Route already refuses it; approval publishes through the real publish transition (publish hook → SyncVideo). The terminal WITHDRAWAL, POST /admin/videos/{id}/reject, calls the seam explicitly rather than waiting on a sweep.

audit.video.block: ipfs_unpinned = ledger rows flipped toward removal
audit.video.unblock: ipfs_rearmed = ledger rows armed toward publication
audit.allowlist: both keys added to audit.allowedMetadataKeys. Counts of ROWS only — never a CID (a public capability handle) or an object key (a media path).

block_lifecycle.best_effort: a mirror error is logged and swallowed: the moderation decision has already landed and the sweep converges regardless, so a mirror hiccup must never fail a takedown

qoe.gap: A31: the client emits playback.start once per session and nothing at the source switch, so a viewer who flipped to IPFS and watched to the end contributed ONE row labelled api-proxy
qoe.fix: usePlaybackQoE restarts its start measurement when the engine moves between delivery ORIGINS, so the next first frame emits a playback.start carrying the new source URL
qoe.classification: server-side, unchanged — the client never names a delivery source. internal/qoe/classify.go files the gateway URL as ipfs-gateway, and api-proxy on the fallback.
qoe.no_new_event_type: qoe_events.event_type is closed by a CHECK constraint (migration 0109), so a playback.source_switch type would need a migration. None was taken.
qoe.not_double_counting: rollups group by (delivery_source, engine, packaging_format), so the second start lands in a different group; per-source playback counts are each right. The viewer really did wait again — hls.js is rebuilt against a different host — so the gateway TTFF is a real measurement nothing else captured.
qoe.origin_scoped: a generation tag, a rung change and every segment change the URL without changing where the bytes come from; an hls.js decline that hands the same URL to native HLS is an engine handover, not a new source. Both pinned by tests.
qoe.no_new_viewer_read: none — the hook already has the session it needs, so useSettledSession was not required

visibility.admin_jobs: media_ipfs_pins joins the overview as jobstatus.QueueIPFSPins, the treatment storage_migrations and cdn_purge_jobs already have: pending = pending+unpinning, running = 0 structurally (a claimed row keeps its state and moves next_attempt_at), done = pinned+unpinned, failed = the dead letters, oldest age measured from next_attempt_at and floored at 0
visibility.no_recent_failures_feed: jobstatus.Failure.ID is a uuid.UUID and this queue is keyed by object_key, a storage path. Widening the shared feed to carry media paths is what RedactDetail exists to prevent, so the dead-letter COUNT rides on the queue row and on the component detail instead.
visibility.still_open: the RUN-LEVEL projection. job_runs carries request_id / correlation_id / trace_id / worker_id and is maintained by per-queue AFTER triggers added in migration 0083; media_ipfs_pins has none, and neither do cdn_purge_jobs or storage_migrations. A mirror retry therefore still cannot be followed through the correlation chain A17 and A35 built. Closing it needs a migration and a trigger.
visibility.migration: NONE TAKEN. 0143 is merged and the set-password slice is renumbering onto 0144; taking 0145 would have left this branch's CI red until that merged. Every column this slice needed already existed.

flipping delivery_ipfs_enabled off stops the 307 on the next request with no restart, and removes the watch page's IPFS control

a pin the ledger never knew is COUNTED on the component and left on the node
